protocol.test: 2025 preseason held out entirely, scored ONCE
protocol.inputs: regular-season cutoff Elo as an explicitly DISCOUNTED prior (discount fit, not assumed), preseason home context, preseason scoring climatology
protocol.excluded: no market input, no post-game information, no regular-season games in the target population
protocol.tiePolicy: ties are excluded from the winner denominator and reported separately — a two-way winner claim has no tie side

mustBeat: home-prior (fit on train preseason home rate)
winner.rationale: a winner claim needs real separation from a coin, not noise; P169's shrink study already found preseason winner skill ≈ 0, so the bar is set where a genuine signal would clear it

mustBeat: regular-season v1 out of domain by ≥ 2.0 points
must not be worse than walk-forward preseason climatology by > 0.25 points
total.threshold: MAE ≤ v1MAE − 2.0 AND MAE ≤ climatologyMAE + 0.25 AND coverage ∈ [0.72, 0.88]
total.rationale: the whole claim is bias correction; if it cannot beat the out-of-domain model by two full points it is not worth a separate version

margin.rationale: removing a phantom home edge must not cost accuracy; a wider-but-honest interval is acceptable, a miscalibrated one is not

honesty: the winner head and the score-distribution heads promote INDEPENDENTLY: a calibrated score range is a real product even where no winner edge exists
the Elo input is a regular-season prior applied at a fitted discount — it is never the target, and its discount is measured rather than chosen
preseason home advantage is FIT, not inherited: the regular-season +48 Elo home constant is not carried over
n is small (98 train / 48 test games) — every promotion here is a bias-correction claim on top of a simple model, never a precision claim
